title: Letter Grade
hints: A `switch` can match ranges of numbers.
Use closed and half-open range patterns for each band, and `default` for anything outside `0...100`.
jsBridge: JS `switch(true)` hacks, or `if` chains, become Swift `switch score { case 90...100: … }`. Range patterns are first-class, and the compiler demands exhaustiveness, so `default` catches invalid scores.

compass.q: `switch (true) { case score >= 90: … }` is a known JS hack. Why does Swift not need it?
If you write `case 90...:` and then `case 80..<90:`, is the order significant? What about overlapping ranges?
Switch on ranges vs a sorted array of thresholds you search through: which is easier to change from remote config?
Would you return a `String` or an enum `Grade`? What does the enum give the UI layer?
